skill.name: post-impl-docs
skill.description: Reviews completed code changes and updates README files, changelogs, docs, and inline docstrings to keep repository documentation aligned with implementation.
skill.summary: Keep repository documentation aligned with completed implementation changes.
skill.author: Consiliency

security_audit.summary: All 79 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown syntax, public documentation links, a placeholder credential, and exception text. The documented commands support repository inspection and documentation checks, with no hidden execution, credential access, exfiltration, or prompt injection. Users should still review generated documentation changes before committing them.

static_findings.snippet: The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/),
- `option` - Optional flag to enable X behavior (default: False)
> **Deprecated**: `old_function()` will be removed in v3.0. Use `new_function()` instead.
Use the `process()` function to process data.
| New feature | Add to Features section | `feat:` entry | If documented |
| Bug fix | No change | `fix:` entry | If affects behavior |
| Breaking change | Update usage examples | `BREAKING:` entry | Update all refs |
| API addition | Add to API section | `feat:` entry | Add API docs |
| Deprecation | Add deprecation note | `deprecate:` entry | Update examples |
| Tests only | No change | `test:` entry | No |

content.value_statement: Code changes often leave README files, changelogs, and docstrings outdated. This skill reviews implementation changes and updates affected documentation using repository conventions.
actual_capabilities: Reviews Git changes to identify documentation impact.
Updates README sections for public features, APIs, installation changes, and breaking changes.
Adds changelog entries in conventional, Keep a Changelog, or simple formats.
Revises docs references and inline docstrings for changed symbols, parameters, returns, errors, and examples.
Produces structured reports for completed updates or changes with no documentation impact.
limitations: Depends on accurate repository diffs and existing documentation.
Does not validate implementation correctness or decide release readiness.
Command examples assume Git and language-specific tools are installed.
Generated documentation and automated changelog entries require human review.

use_cases.title: Document a completed feature
use_cases.description: Update README sections, changelog entries, reference pages, and docstrings after adding a public feature.

use_cases.title: Prepare a pull request
use_cases.description: Review implementation changes and make affected documentation consistent before opening or merging a pull request.

use_cases.title: Standardize documentation workflows
use_cases.description: Apply shared changelog and docstring conventions after automated implementation tasks.

prompt_templates.title: Update documentation for one change
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the latest implementation diff. Update only the README, changelog, docs, and docstrings affected by the change. Summarize every edit.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of one completed change

prompt_templates.title: Refresh API documentation
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare the changed public API with current documentation. Update signatures, parameters, return values, errors, and examples while preserving repository style. Report unresolved gaps.

prompt_templates.title: Document a breaking release
prompt_templates.prompt: Document the breaking change between [base_ref] and [head_ref]. Update usage examples, migration guidance, deprecation notes, docstrings, and the changelog. Identify references needing manual review.

prompt_templates.title: Audit documentation across a release
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit documentation for all changes between [base_ref] and [head_ref]. Review README, changelog, docs, and docstrings. Apply evidence-supported updates and run available documentation checks. Return a file-by-file impact summary.

output_examples.input: A new public authentication method was added with one configuration option.
output: README: Added the authentication method and configuration option.
CHANGELOG: Added a feature entry under the unreleased section.
Docstrings: Updated the public method parameters and example.

output_examples.input: An internal cache was refactored without changing public behavior.
output_examples.output: No documentation changes were needed because the refactor did not affect public behavior, APIs, installation, or configuration.

output_examples.input: A public method was renamed and the previous name was deprecated.
output: README: Replaced usage examples and added a migration note.
CHANGELOG: Recorded the rename and deprecation.
Docs: Updated references to the previous method name.

best_practices: Review the implementation diff before editing documentation.
Match existing repository structure, terminology, and formatting.
Run relevant documentation tests and inspect the final diff.
anti_patterns: Do not document internal refactors as public features.
Do not replace verified examples with untested assumptions.
Do not add changelog entries for formatting-only or documentation-only changes.

faq.question: What files can this skill update?
faq.answer: It can update README files, changelogs, documentation folders, and inline docstrings affected by implementation changes.

faq.question: Which changelog formats are supported?
faq.answer: It provides guidance for conventional changelogs, Keep a Changelog, and simple project changelogs.

faq.question: Can I limit the documentation scope?
faq.answer: Yes. Configuration variables can enable or disable README, changelog, documentation folder, and docstring updates.

faq.question: Does the skill change functional source code?
faq.answer: It targets documentation and inline docstrings. Review the diff to ensure no functional code changes are introduced.

faq.question: Does the skill commit changes automatically?
faq.answer: The skill defines a COMMIT_DOCS option, but repository permissions and the invoking workflow control commit behavior.

faq.question: How should generated updates be verified?
faq.answer: Review the final diff, confirm examples match current APIs, and run available doctest or documentation checks.
